claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: an actual 18.3 km against a recommended 15.7 km is 2.60 km, far above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, and POL-RD-22 measures the deviation on the recorded distances precisely so that the sparse trace is not used to understate the route.

The trace confirms the route the rider describes, so there is no dispute about which way the driver went: the vehicle is on the Tampines Expressway from 14:18:41 and on Braddell Road from 14:29:41, and it rejoins the recommended route only at Toa Payoh Lorong 6 at 14:40:41 — exactly the deviation and rejoin events the trip record logs.

The driver's traffic excuse is not made out on this record. The only advisory is LTA-TI-260905-2467, a ROADWORK on the Pan-Island Expressway (towards Tuas) after the Tampines Avenue 10 exit, with an active window of 2026-09-05 23:00 to 2026-09-06 05:00 — hours after this trip, which ran 14:16:11 to 14:42:11. It therefore does not overlap the trip window and does not intersect the recommended route as driven, so under POL-RD-23 the reroute is not traffic-justified and the counter-statement's 'PIE got roadworks' justifies nothing.

The driver also gave the rider no notice of the deviation: the chat log holds zero messages and the trip record records no in-app calls, while POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat, or verbally with a trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. A verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established (POL-GEN-26), so the contact limb fails alongside the traffic limb — the rider was taken the long way round and told nothing.

A deviation that is not traffic-justified and exceeds 1 km falls in row (d) of POL-RD-24, which pays the excess distance fare in full: 2.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.87 SGD, computed without surge. I do not put the rider's case above the policy's own measure — the 6.00 SGD the rider asks is the amount contested, not the matrix figure — but on this record 1.87 SGD is money the rider should not be carrying, and on the driver's own version (informed, but unjustified) row (b) yields the same sum.

Because the established deviation is 2.60 km and POL-RD-25 lets an AI ruling stand only where the deviation is 2 km or less, this case must go to a human reviewer. That is the outcome the policy provides, and it is not a loss to the rider: under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and the amount is held rather than finally collected, and the findings above — an over-tolerance deviation, no justifying advisory, and no notice — stand as the case file the reviewer works from.

The deviation is measured under POL-RD-22 on the platform's recorded distances, not on the GPS trace: trip_record.actual_distance_km (18.3 km) minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km (15.7 km) is 2.60 km, more than double the 1.0 km tolerance. The driver-device trace cannot displace that figure — POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length, and EV-GPS-05015's 15.434 km trace_distance_km is expressly not a re-measurement — so the 1.0 km tolerance limb of POL-RD-24 is not available to the driver on this record, and the deviation is over POL-RD-25's 2.0 km ceiling as well.

Because the deviation (2.60 km) is over the 2.0 km ceiling in POL-RD-25, no AI ruling on this route deviation can stand and the case must be escalated: that 2 km limb is the version settled by Ryde (C1) which sent DISP-001's 4.3 km deviation to a human, and 2.60 km falls on the same side of the line. Escalation is the outcome that protects the driver: under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE is terminal, replaces any ruling, issues no monetary outcome, and holds the amount while a human reviews it — so the rider's $6.00 is not returned and the 21.56 SGD already charged (refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is left undisturbed at this stage.

Even if this case were rulable, the rider's pleaded $6.00 is more than three times anything the route-deviation matrix can award: POL-RD-24 moves only the excess distance fare, at the base per-km rate without surge, which on this trip is 2.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.87 SGD. A claim for the whole contested amount, or anything approaching it, is unsupported by the arithmetic the policy sets.

The driver's own explanation — that PIE roadworks forced the reroute — is not made out on this record: the only TRAFFIC_ADVISORY on file (a ROADWORK on the PIE towards Tuas after Tampines Ave 10 Exit) is valid 23:00-05:00, while this trip ran 14:16-14:42, so it does not overlap the trip window and POL-RD-23's overlap requirement is not met; an assertion of traffic with no overlapping data does not justify a reroute. That failure does not hand the rider a ruling on this record: it is precisely the merits question that POL-RD-25 reserves to the human reviewer to whom this case goes.
